title: inspect: expose init container information
body:
## Description

Add `IsInitCtr` and `InitContainerType` fields to `podman container inspect`
output so init containers can be distinguished from regular containers.

This exposes the init-container information that Podman already tracks
internally.

Fixes: #29811

## Testing

- Added e2e coverage for init-container inspect output.
- Verified normal containers report `IsInitCtr: false`.
- Verified init containers report `IsInitCtr: true`.
- Verified `InitContainerType` is exposed for init containers.

## Documentation

Updated `podman-container-inspect` documentation for the new fields.

Hi @BartSimpson001  

This is my first review in the Podman repository. Please correct me if I am missing anything as a Reviewer.

I tested the behavior locally:
- Without this patch, querying `--format '{{.IsInitCtr}}'` fails with `can't evaluate field IsInitCtr in type interface {}` (reproducing the exact gap).
- The additions to `InspectContainerData` and the e2e test in `container_inspect_test.go` address this cleanly.

As a small suggestion to make the documentation even more practical, could we also add a short example under the `## EXAMPLES` section in `podman-container-inspect.1.md.in` (around line 331, right before `## SEE ALSO`)?

Something like:

````markdown
Inspect the specified container to check whether it is an init container and its type.
```
$ podman container inspect my-init-ctr --format "{{.IsInitCtr}} {{.InitContainerType}}"
true always
```
